title: The thermal lever against the duplicate-cell floor: how large a temperature spread a lifetime divergence needs, and how large a module offers
description: Pre-registered calculation of how large a steady temperature difference between nominally identical lithium-ion cells two published temperature-dependent ageing laws need to produce a lifetime difference as large as the duplicate-cell floor of the Geslin et al. dynamic-cycling dataset (mean 3.0 %, 95th percentile 8.7 %, worst of eight 4.1 % at 90 % state of health), and how large a temperature difference a module at 35 C offers: an eight-cell lumped network of LG M50 21700 cells and a resolved scikit-fem cell, at average rates from C/16 to 2C and convection coefficients of 5, 10 and 25 W/(m2 K). Predictions were committed and pushed before any lever or spread was computed. Code under the MIT licence; results, figure and note under CC BY 4.0.
